LESSON: READING 5.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY (CLASS READER)

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader), part of Strand 5 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What makes stories interesting to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify dialogue and repetition in a short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the importance of repetition and dialogue in a short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the role of dialogue and repetition in fiction writing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify dialogue and repetition in a short story,

   Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. explain the importance of repetition and dialogue in a short story,

   Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge the role of dialogue and repetition in fiction writing.

   Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch plays that have characters talking to one another and repeating certain lines or sentences from a digital device,

2. read a short story and work with peers to retell

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch plays that have characters talking to one another and repeating certain lines or sentences from a digital device,
2. read a short story and work with peers to retell

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: It is enhanced as the learner discusses the relationship between characters in a short story

in real life.

Values:
Unity: It is promoted as the learner displays team spirit when role playing a dialogue in the short story read.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peace education: It is developed as the learner appreciates the opinion of their peers as they engage in dialogue.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the concepts learnt in literary works to learning literary works in Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify dialogue and repetition in a short story,
2. explain the importance of repetition and dialogue in a short story,
3. acknowledge the role of dialogue and repetition in fiction writing.

Remember the key question: What makes stories interesting to read?
